panels.text: Before leaving for his holiday, Alexander Fleming inoculated staphylococci on culture plates and left them on a bench in a corner of his laboratory.
On his return, he noticed that one culture was contaminated with a fungus. The staphylococci colonies immediately surrounding the fungus had been destroyed, whereas colonies farther away were normal.
He famously remarked "That's funny". He grew the mould in a pure culture and found that the culture broth contained an antibacterial substance.
His discovery in 1928 was of what was later named benzylpenicillin, from the mould Penicillium rubens.
